verdicts.factCheck: PositionManager source. I fetched the Sourcify record of 0xbD216513d74C8cf14cf4747E6AaA6420FF64ee9e on Ethereum (creation and runtime match, solc 0.8.26). In src/PositionManager.sol, _handleAction (lines 197 to 286) has branches for INCREASE_LIQUIDITY, INCREASE_LIQUIDITY_FROM_DELTAS, DECREASE_LIQUIDITY, MINT_POSITION, MINT_POSITION_FROM_DELTAS, BURN_POSITION, SETTLE_PAIR, TAKE_PAIR, SETTLE, TAKE, CLOSE_CURRENCY, CLEAR_OR_TAKE, SWEEP, WRAP and UNWRAP and ends with revert UnsupportedAction(action). _clearOrTake (lines 474 to 484) calls poolManager.clear when the credit is at most amountMax. src/libraries/Actions.sol defines MINT_6909 as 0x17 and BURN_6909 as 0x18 under the comment that they are not supported in the position manager or router. Chain. On 2026-11-23 I sent eth_call of modifyLiquidities with the single action 0x17 from an unrelated account to the PositionManager of each of the 21 networks, using the endpoints in networks.json. All 21 revert with 0x5cda29d7 followed by 0x17. I computed 0x5cda29d7 as the selector of UnsupportedAction(uint256). Action 0x18 gives the same error with 0x18 on 20 networks. The Avalanche endpoint rate limited that one call. eth_getCode returns 23,877 bytes on 19 networks and 19,965 bytes on Elysium and HyperEVM. Simulations from the position owner, built with my own encoder. Celo, https://forno.celo.org, blocks 83,532,678 and 83,533,160, position 178 (G$ and cUSD, owner 0xf18f712b760732cde4d1835673b98b2c7978b3a8): decrease with TAKE_PAIR, with TAKE of each side and with CLOSE_CURRENCY all revert with 0x90bfb865 carrying the G$ address and selector a9059cbb. MINT_6909 reverts with UnsupportedAction(0x17). Leaving the G$ delta open reverts with 0x5212cba1. Decrease or burn, TAKE of cUSD and CLEAR_OR_TAKE of G$ with the maximum amount return without error. Decrease, TAKE of cUSD, MINT_POSITION_FROM_DELTAS into ticks -106690 to 887270 and CLEAR_OR_TAKE return without error, and a multicall that reads the result shows new token 605 with liquidity 100,918,514,712,628,699,620 owned by the same account and the old token at zero. The same calls from an unrelated account revert with NotApproved. Polygon, https://polygon.drpc.org, blocks 97,818,649 to 97,818,969, position 60652 (WETH and VCNT): the full removal shows the same pattern, and sequence B leaves new token 159444 with liquidity 1,034,117,479,046,245,712. transferLimitAmountRemaining(PoolManager) was 6.1256 VCNT at that time, so nobody had used up the allowance. Removals of 50, 10 and 2 percent of position 60652 with TAKE_PAIR succeed today, and position 14963 exits in full. The full removal of 60652 fails today because its VCNT side is larger than the allowance. I then found the storage slot of the daily total of the PoolManager in the plugin 0xf58fed40fba1ab7aa7ffc160b863bedd998386a7 with a prestate trace of a 1 VCNT transfer (slot 0x177da5a421dc5b34775004a7c8f5481d6125d6eba1e5f5ef95b99364e3e7eb64) and set it to minus 6 VCNT by state override. With that override transferLimitAmountRemaining returns 0, a transfer of one base unit from the PoolManager reverts with 0x1b97a875, a 2 percent removal of 60652 and the full removal of 14963 with TAKE_PAIR revert, and sequences A and B still succeed. That state is the one F-072 shows an ordinary account can produce with about 6.13 VCNT of net outflow per day. Monad, https://rpc.monad.xyz, block 124,707,777, position 651334 with the code of 0xe7cd86e13ac4309349f30b3435a9d337750fc82d replaced by 0x5f5ffd: same pattern. SDK. I fetched PositionManager.ts and utils/v4Planner.ts from the main branch of Uniswap/sdks. removeCallParameters (lines 334 to 399) adds a burn or a decrease and then addTakePair. collectCallParameters (lines 407 to 430) adds a decrease by zero and addTakePair. The Actions enum (lines 30 to 66) has INCREASE_LIQUIDITY_FROM_DELTAS, MINT_POSITION_FROM_DELTAS, CLEAR_OR_TAKE and WRAP as comments and no entry for 0x17 or 0x18. Not rechecked: the counts of ViciCoin and G$ pools with PositionManager positions (8 of 15 and 5 of 8), the 7.9 million dollar figure taken from F-061, the Arc simulation, and which calldata the hosted Uniswap web application sends for a removal.
verdicts.codeCheck: I traced the path in this repository. modifyLiquidity records the position under msg.sender (src/PoolManager.sol:161) and credits the removal to msg.sender (line 183), so a position made through a periphery contract can be closed only by that contract. unlock reverts with CurrencyNotSettled when any delta is left (src/PoolManager.sol:112), which matches the 0x5212cba1 revert seen when the blocked side is left open. take debits the caller and then calls currency.transfer (src/PoolManager.sol:291-297). The ERC-20 branch makes the call at src/types/Currency.sol:64-73 and reverts with the wrapped error when the token call fails or returns anything other than nothing or a 32 byte true (lines 82-86). The wrapped error carries the token address and selector a9059cbb, which is the revert data seen on Celo, Polygon and Monad. One failed take reverts the whole modifyLiquidities call, so the other currency stays in the pool too. clear requires the amount to equal the caller's positive delta and then erases it with no token call and no claim (src/PoolManager.sol:310-319). mint debits the caller's delta and calls _mint with no token call (src/PoolManager.sol:322-329, src/ERC6909.sol:79-83), so core can pay a blocked currency as a claim. I looked for a guard that changes this and found none: the msg.value check in _settle (line 356), the synced currency check in collectProtocolFees (src/ProtocolFees.sol:49-52) and the int128 casts (src/libraries/SafeCast.sol:56-59) play no part in a removal. Core behaves as written. The missing route is in the PositionManager, which is outside src/.
verdicts.corrections: The actor value unprivileged is right for Polygon (chain 137) alone, where F-072 lets any account use up the ViciCoin allowance. On the other 20 networks in chainIds a token must first refuse transfers from the PoolManager, and that needs the token issuer (G$ on Celo, the wrapped stock tokens on Monad, TIP-20 policies on Tempo). The chainIds list should be read as where the PositionManager lacks the action, and the unprivileged trigger exists on one network. The Polygon evidence needs one change. Position 60652 fails to close in full today because its VCNT side exceeds the 6 VCNT daily allowance, with 6.1256 VCNT of allowance still open. Removals of 50, 10 and 2 percent succeed with TAKE_PAIR, which the SDK can build through liquidityPercentage. The block for every size appears only after the allowance is used up, which I reproduced with a state override. The freeze applies to providers who rely on interface-built calldata. An owner who sends modifyLiquidities by hand can leave with the other currency through sequence B at any time, or by INCREASE_LIQUIDITY_FROM_DELTAS into another position of the same pool. No funds reach the attacker. The amounts under the unprivileged trigger are small: the PoolManager on Polygon held 11.35 VCNT, about 206 USD. The finding is about periphery code and a third party token rule. It does not follow from a difference between a network and Ethereum, and the same PositionManager behaviour exists on Ethereum. It overlaps F-072, F-056 and F-061 and adds to them the fact that the paired currency is locked for interface users. SDK line numbers: removeCallParameters ends at line 399 and collectCallParameters spans lines 407 to 430 in the file I fetched. Unconfirmed link: what the hosted Uniswap interface sends for a removal.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Reading of the claim transfer and burn checks in this repository: src/ERC6909.sol:35-48 (transferFrom), src/ERC6909Claims.sol:13-22 (_burnFrom), src/PoolManager.sol:322-336 (mint and burn), src/types/Currency.sol:110-118 (toId and fromId), src/libraries/SafeCast.sol:56-59.
clearedSpotChecks.note: I read the same lines. transferFrom skips the allowance step only for the sender or an operator of the sender and otherwise writes allowed minus amount with checked arithmetic (src/ERC6909.sol:36-39). Both balance updates are checked (lines 41 and 43). _burnFrom applies the same test to from (src/ERC6909Claims.sol:13-22). burn credits msg.sender and burns from the named account (src/PoolManager.sol:332-336). mint debits msg.sender and its amount is below 2^127 because of src/libraries/SafeCast.sol:56-59. The unchecked block in mint covers the negation only, and the addition in _mint is checked (src/ERC6909.sol:79-83). fromId truncates to 160 bits (src/types/Currency.sol:116-118). I added one check: the selectors the PoolManager sends to addresses a caller names (the ten IHooks functions, unlockCallback, transfer(address,uint256), balanceOf(address)) do not equal any claim selector (0x095bcdb6, 0xfe99049a, 0x426a8493, 0x558a7297, 0xf5298aca, 0x156e29f6), and src/ has no fallback or receive, so an approval given to the PoolManager itself cannot be used through take, sync or a hook call that names the PoolManager.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Do the shared contracts that run command lists or batches for any caller hold an approval? I matched every operator and spender address of all 21 networks against Multicall3, Multicall2, Permit2, the Across MulticallHandler, the 1inch v6 router, the 0x exchange proxy and AllowanceHolder, the CoW settlement contract, the three ERC-4337 EntryPoint versions, the Safe MultiSend contracts, the LiFi diamond, the Kyber meta router, CreateX and every Uniswap contract listed in networks.json.
clearedSpotChecks.note: I fetched both Sourcify records (match) and listed every external call. On Base the Dispatcher calls Permit2, the v3 position manager, the v4 PositionManager, itself and poolManager.initialize, and V4Router._handleAction rejects every action outside the swaps, SETTLE_ALL, TAKE_ALL, SETTLE, TAKE and TAKE_PORTION. The Robinhood Chain router is a later version and the cleared text leaves out one branch: command ACROSS_V4_DEPOSIT_V3 (Dispatcher.sol:311-312, ChainedActions.sol:19-57) calls balanceOf(address) and approve(address,uint256) on an inputToken the caller names and then SPOKE_POOL.depositV3. With the PoolManager as inputToken these calls revert, because the PoolManager has neither selector. I confirmed by eth_call that the PoolManagers on Robinhood Chain, Base and Ethereum revert on 0xa9059cbb, 0x23b872dd, 0x095ea7b3 and 0x70a08231. Payments use ERC-20 transfer and Permit2 only. isOperator(0xd7c7200e8d781013e16db8418ded4767a5beb598, router) on Robinhood Chain returns true as stated. No path reaches burn or the ERC-6909 transferFrom. The PositionManager source has no such call either. The clearance stands and its description should add the Across branch.

Largest by number of owners: 0x639cfe8cb8023d9f996f3100722e8691ac751b0b (11), PrismataRouter 0x45b890060fbbbda666b9542297caafff91e697c9 (7), 0xbc22993a15e16acbf12873f234510d35948f7a59 (5), 0x4531332adecf255c66b5bf6485db73f894ed93d2 (4), BunniHub 0x000000dceb71f3107909b1b748424349bfde5493 (3), Panoptic SemiFungiblePositionManager 0x0000000000000aabbcfca8100a9ee78124e97b33 (3). 54 approving owners hold claims in 249 owner and id pairs, about 28,850 USD in the tokens I could price and 113 pairs unpriced.
clearedSpotChecks.note: I rechecked the two largest exposures. TurbineLiquidityRouter (Sourcify match): unlockCallback and _removeLiquidityCallback both require msg.sender to be the PoolManager (lines 271 and 547), the callback pulls the LP tokens with Permit2 permitTransferFrom from the named caller before the two burns of the hook's claims (lines 551-561), removeLiquidity is limited to the settler (line 465), and an intent can be submitted only by its owner with a signature that verifies for the owner (lines 133 and 157). The PoolManager calls unlockCallback only on the account that called unlock (src/PoolManager.sol:110), so no other account can feed data to the delegatecall at line 272. Contract 0x63e962b4102e8bac865ed84d2a678a0b65b64ab0 (1,302 bytes, disassembled here): unlockCallback has no CALLER check, reads balanceOf(tx.origin, id) at pc 0x124-0x14a, calls burn with ORIGIN as from at pc 0x159-0x184 and pays ORIGIN or the fixed address 0x9b19f7f92e60c1fe20d6080ec390c7aa6bb72811, so only a transaction signed by the owner moves the owner's claims. I did not recheck the unverified routers 0xbc22993a, 0x4531332a, 0xad445acd or proxy 0x37bfb8ac, which the cleared text names as its limit.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Robinhood Chain census: 491 logs (226 OperatorSet, 265 Approval) from block 0 to 121,284,941. 143 operator addresses and 28 spender addresses. 143 addresses hold a live approval: 134 contracts, 3 delegated accounts, 6 accounts without code. Largest: 0x2834c56d948f063564ff0a3c29483db50c73045a holds an unlimited allowance from 120 owners (40 each on the ids of three tokens), 0x3e38af660efeaba4efa38b1d3dbc05baf12e0c60 is operator for 15 owners, three 47,585 byte hooks have 6 or 7 owners each, HookWallRewards 0x5322963d82ffc9fd18953578e08757d0faa61b27 has 8 allowances. 84 owners hold claims in 2,170 pairs, about 6,288 USD priced and 2,100 pairs unpriced.
clearedSpotChecks.note: The answer holds and the stated reason for 0x2834c56d948f063564ff0a3c29483db50c73045a is wrong. The contract does call PoolManager.burn. Its bytecode holds the strings burn(address,uint256,uint256), mint(address,uint256,uint256), burn(address,address,uint256), mint(address,address,uint256), unlock(bytes) and lock(bytes) and hashes them at run time (pc 0x163c-0x17ae, KECCAK256 at 0x0c63), so a search for the constant 0xf5298aca misses the call. I read the code. redeem(address,uint256,bytes32) at 0x0824, transferToken(address,address,uint256,bytes32) at 0x022c and the two deposit entries at 0x0cdc each store CALLER as the account of the request (pc 0x08b3-0x08df, 0x03b0, 0x0e6a). The callback at 0x0eea requires the caller to be the PoolManager, an in-flight flag in slot 1 and slot 2 equal to the hash of the data, and the redeem branch at 0x12f3-0x1399 burns from that account and takes to the same account. An unrelated caller therefore cannot spend the 120 allowances. The clearance should be restated with this reason.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Caller test of unlockCallback. For each of 714 approved contracts the same calldata was sent once with from set to the PoolManager and once from an unrelated account, with five payloads. A contract whose callback has no caller check can be driven by any account that has unlocked the PoolManager itself.
clearedSpotChecks.note: I listed the 17 contracts from the guard output and rechecked the three whose exclusion rests on the absence of a burn or transferFrom constant. None holds the constants or the signature strings. The BNB Smart Chain contract 0x46e0a3cb7389ca740477cd5e05a08e944b7280ea (1,253 bytes, read in full) has no CALLER or ORIGIN opcode. Its functions send its native balance to an immutable owner, call setOperator(address(this), true) on the PoolManager, which makes it an operator of itself only, and call two selectors (0xfa2f490e and 0x2dad6442) on the PoolManager. The two Robinhood Chain test contracts have no such string either.

leads.question: Which approved operator or spender contracts build the burn or transferFrom selector at run time (signature strings such as burn(address,uint256,uint256) hashed in code, or a selector taken from calldata), and for each of them is the debited account always the caller?
leads.why: The census excluded contracts by searching bytecode for the constants 0xf5298aca and 0xfe99049a. That test missed 0x2834c56d948f063564ff0a3c29483db50c73045a on Robinhood Chain, which holds 120 unlimited allowances and calls burn through a hashed string. My reading clears that contract, and the same test was the stated reason elsewhere. A string search over all approved bytecode and a trace of each hit would close the gap.

leads.question: What calldata does the hosted Uniswap interface or its liquidity API return for a removal when a simulation of TAKE_PAIR fails, and does any widely used front end offer MINT_POSITION_FROM_DELTAS or CLEAR_OR_TAKE?
leads.why: The freeze of the paired currency in this unit's finding is confirmed for calldata built with the published SDK. Whether real users are stuck depends on the interface, which neither the researcher nor I captured.
